  name: "Gradient-Based Optimization (GCG Suffix Attack)",
  objective: "Automatically discovers adversarial suffixes that cause aligned models to comply with harmful requests, by using gradient access to a (usually open-weight) surrogate model to iteratively refine token candidates that maximize compliance likelihood. Implements and extends Zou et al.'s Greedy Coordinate Gradient attack [R02], the founding result of optimization-based jailbreaking.",
  mechanism: "Established layer: GCG optimizes a discrete token suffix S appended to a harmful request D, maximizing P(model accepts D+S) — operationalized as the probability of an affirmative prefix ('Sure, here is…'). Because the suffix space is discrete, Zou et al. use gradients w.r.t. one-hot token embeddings to rank candidate substitutions at each position, then greedily accept the best candidate that keeps a small set of suffixes in play (beam-ish search) [R02]. Two findings made the result foundational: transferability — suffixes optimized on open models (Llama 2, Vicuna, Guanaco era) transferred to closed targets including GPT-3.5/4-class models at nontrivial rates — and universality — one suffix works across many prompts. Subsequent literature is a family tree: PAIR replaces gradients with an attacker LLM loop [R07], TAP adds tree search over that loop [R08], AutoDAN uses genetic search for readable (low-perplexity) jailbreaks [R09], simple adaptive attacks (GCG with restarts + affirmative-prefix forcing) broke most then-current open-model defenses [R15], and fine-tuning on a handful of GCG-derived examples generalizes the bypass [R18]. HYPOTHESIS (2026 frontier status): suffix efficacy on current top tiers (GPT-5.6-class, Claude Opus 5-class, Gemini 3.1 Pro-class) is materially lower than 2023-2024 transfer rates — supported by the direction of published defensive investment [R30][R31] but without public per-model numbers; label ESTIMATE.",
  mitigation: "Published defensive line: randomized smoothing / paraphrase-based prompt and output perturbation (SmoothLLM [R36]); paraphrasing and retokenization defenses with their adaptive-attack evaluations [R37]; adversarial training on suffix corpora; instruction-hierarchy training [R31]; constitutional/output classifiers [R30]. Serving hygiene: do not expose logprobs (the API misuses documented by Nasr et al. — logit-bias + forward-logprob system-prompt reconstruction — show logit-adjacent surfaces are attack surfaces [R34]); rate-limit and cluster-monitor suffix-like gibberish traffic (high-perplexity detection catches classic GCG but not AutoDAN-class readable attacks [R09]).   highLevelResearchCommentary: {
    content: "GCG's lasting contribution is epistemic: it demonstrated that alignment lives in a thin, searchable shell over capabilities, and everything since — attacker-LLM loops [R07][R08], readable evolution [R09], adaptive breaks of early defenses [R15], soft-prompt extremity [R16], fine-tune generalization [R18] — has mapped that shell's geography at increasing realism.
